subject: Deployment path & isolation evidence — HealthGrid POC (next steps)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Nguyen <laura@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Deployment path & isolation evidence — HealthGrid POC (next steps)

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the time this morning — great conversation and helpful context on HealthGrid’s security must-haves. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align engineering and procurement:  

What we heard (priority order):
- Primary: strict tenant isolation and control-plane residency in a customer-dedicated environment (no co-mingled metadata)
- Secondary: KMS/HSM-backed key control, auditable access logs with 90+ days retention, and network egress controls to your whitelisted destinations
- Nice-to-have: on-prem option for the busiest workloads (for later phases)

Deployment options we discussed (short):
- Hosted API: fastest to run, multi-tenant control plane, good for initial feature tests but limited for strict custody requirements
- Dedicated capacity: single-tenant GPU pools managed by Redwood with customer data isolation and optional private peering; control plane still hosted unless Private deployed
- Private VPC (VPC or on-prem): customer-managed network and optional private control plane; most alignment with HealthGrid’s custody/regulatory bar

Evidence & artifacts you asked for (we’ll prepare):
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted sections as appropriate)
- Network topology and egress/ingress diagram for Dedicated and Private variants
- Keystore residency statement + KMS/HSM integration notes
- Audit-log schema and sample log entries (events, retention)
- Operational runbook for canary/fallback between Dedicated and Hosted

What we need from you to qualify the path:
1) Confirmation of the absolute must-have vs nice-to-have items (e.g., is a private control plane mandatory or is dedicated capacity acceptable if it includes private peering + strict log segregation?)
2) List of the technical owners who will review the artifacts (security, infra, procurement) and the preferred timeline for review (you mentioned a 12/1 decision goal on the call)
3) Any compliance/GRC artifacts you want us to pre-populate into your questionnaire (happy to fill the Red Team/infra sections)

Attached is a working checklist we’ll populate: isolation-evidence-checklist.xlsx — I’ll add the SOC2 and network diagram links as soon as they’re available.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll schedule a short follow-up workshop with our solutions engineer (Marissa) to walk the Dedicated and Private VPC artifacts — propose next Tue/Wed (30–45m)
- Marissa will draft a short mutual action plan with owners and dates once we hear back on priorities

If the control plane residency is non-negotiable, flag that explicitly and I’ll pull in our Private deployment lead to scope a tighter SOW.

Thanks — speak soon.

Karthik Iyer
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0183

Attachment: isolation-evidence-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Laura Nguyen <laura@healthgrid.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Susan Miles <susan.miles@healthgrid.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment path & isolation evidence — HealthGrid POC (next steps)

Karthik —

Thanks for the recap, that’s helpful. A few quick clarifications from my side before we lock the workshop slot:

1) Control plane residency: for production traffic handling PHI-derived requests, we need an option where the control plane can be hosted within our VPC (or on-prem) and not shared across customers. If Dedicated can offer that tenancy model we should consider it, but it sounded like Dedicated still uses Redwood’s control plane. Can you confirm exactly what isolation Dedicated provides for metadata and model artifacts?

2) Audit logs & retention: 90 days is the minimum. Logs must be searchable by our security team and consumable via S3 or a syslog endpoint. Will Redwood provide a log delivery or do we need to poll an API?

3) Disk/tensor storage at rest: are intermediate tensors persisted on disk for Dedicated? If so, are they encrypted with a per-tenant key?

4) Timeline: yes, our procurement lead (Susan Miles) is aiming for a decision by 2026-12-01. We’ll need the artifacts by 11/24 to allow a two-week security review.

I attached our updated GRC questionnaire — could you have Marissa fill in the infra/security sections we discussed?

—Laura
Laura Nguyen
Head of Security Engineering
HealthGrid Inc
laura@healthgrid.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

Attachment: GRC_questionnaire_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Nguyen <laura@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Susan Miles <susan.miles@healthgrid.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment path & isolation evidence — HealthGrid POC (next steps)

Laura — thanks, and appreciate the timeframe. Quick answers and an action plan:  

Answers (short):
- Dedicated capacity: provides single-tenant GPU pools and per-tenant data partitions. The control plane (deployment orchestration, billing, model registry) remains in Redwood-hosted control plane by default. We can offer a Private control plane as an add-on (customer-managed VPC or on-prem) for production PHI — this is the route that satisfies your "no shared control plane" requirement.
- Audit logs: Redwood can push logs to an S3 endpoint or forward to a syslog/collection endpoint. We’ll provide searchable log samples and an S3 delivery example.
- Tensor/disk encryption: For Dedicated we encrypt at-rest using per-tenant keys. For Private deployments, keys can be customer-managed in their KMS/HSM. Intermediate KV cache can be configured to only reside in memory for stricter profiles (we’ll document tradeoffs).

Proposed mutual action plan (dates aligned to your 12/1 decision):
- By 11/15: Redwood delivers SOC2 redacted report + keystore residency note + sample audit log (Marissa)
- By 11/18: Network topology diagrams for Dedicated and Private VPC + list of required firewall rules (Marissa)
- 11/19–11/20: 45m technical workshop (Marissa + Redwood infra lead) to walk artifacts and answer infra questions
- By 11/24: Redwood to return the completed infra/security sections of your GRC questionnaire
- 11/29: Final clarifications and SOW outline for Private control plane (if selected)

Owners:
- Redwood security & artifact delivery: Marissa Cole (marissa@redwood.ai)
- Solution design and private control plane scope: Ben Carter (ben@redwood.ai)
- HealthGrid reviewers: Laura Nguyen (security) and Susan Miles (procurement)

Next actions I’ll take now:
- Marissa will start filling the GRC spreadsheet and upload the SOC2 redacted and log sample to the Drive link below (I’ll share access).
- I’ll send an invite for the 11/19/20 workshop (please indicate preferred time window)

If a private control plane is required, we’ll prep a short scope doc and a ballpark T&M estimate for the SOW in parallel — want to surface any cost/time impacts up-front.

Would you like Marissa to start with the SOC2 & logs or the network diagrams first? We’ll prioritize based on your review order.

Thanks — Karthik

Karthik Iyer
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0183
